topic: Pebble-certified rank-two counterfactual recovery and singular-margin upper guarantees. Fix finite T,C, rank two, deterministic untreated masks S_c with |S_c|>=3 and positive cohort shares; impose bounded positive loading covariances, local signal eigengaps, factor/loadings, conditional homoskedastic outcome-uncorrelated errors, and a common 4+delta moment radius. Replace each mask by |S_c|-2 anchor triples. Prove that the published rank-two count certificate is sufficient for all missing cohort-time untreated means to be complete-observed-law functionals, while certificate failure implies generic factor-plane ambiguity only and does not imply causal-target nonidentification under the frozen primitives. Give the O(Tm) background pebble certificate and the strict O3 containment witness for masks 123,145,256,346. For relation singular margin s in [s_N,2s_N], prove the radius-adaptive covariance-PCA squared-risk upper bound min{1,4 b_lambda^2,K/(N s_N^2)} and uniformly honest profile-inversion rectangle upper half-width min{b_lambda,C_alpha min(1,1/(sqrt(N)s_N))}; N s_N^2 divergence is sufficient but not necessary for consistency. Record the legal tight-radius zero-target family and nonempty-shell counterexample as obstructions to universal identification converses, positive minimax/width lower frontiers, and a necessary consistency threshold. A frontier-scale testing pair on a separately justified quantitatively nondegenerate subclass remains open and is not assumed.

open_problems.open_problem: For rank-two interactive-fixed-effect panels with deterministic cohort masks, is every missing untreated cohort-time mean an entire-observed-law functional exactly when the anchor-triple hypergraph contains a spanning (1,2)-tight subhypergraph?

source_refs.claim: Their fixed-T spectral method identifies counterfactual matrix means under general missingness using overlap connectivity, but does not state the proposed rank-two tight-hypergraph iff frontier.
source_refs.author: Lihua Lei and Brad Ross

source_refs.claim: They characterize generic entry completability through the determinantal matroid, Jacobians, stresses, and polynomial circuits.
source_refs.author: Franz J. Király, Louis Theran, and Ryota Tomioka

source_refs.claim: They characterize sparse hypergraph matroids and give pebble games for recognition, extraction, and tight-component detection.
source_refs.author: Ileana Streinu and Louis Theran

source_refs.excerpt: above the margin threshold, rank-r completion point-identifies all cohort-time untreated counterfactual cells
that paper already gives tangent/projection identification conditions and a nonrecoverability result

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published work supplies three separate components: spectral recovery under overlap, generic determinantal-matroid completion, and abstract sparse-hypergraph pebble games. The rejected prior proposal did not connect them through an invariant mask-only object and conflated an abstract local tangent criterion with model-wide recovery. New work must prove that the rank-two anchor relations represent the (1,2)-sparsity matroid after quotienting change-of-basis invariance, then lift every residual motion on a failing mask to two legal factor/loading/error distributions with the same complete observed law.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An iff identification theorem, an O(Tm) pebble-game certificate, and for every failing mask an explicit pair of admissible rank-two data-generating processes with identical observed laws but different missing untreated means.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation arc from systematically missing short-panel counterfactuals to mask-dependent spectral identification and implementable recovery.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Counterfactual outcomes are systematically missing in short panels -> low-rank factors connect cohort-specific observed outcome sets -> overlap geometry permits recovery -> characterize the exact rank-two mask frontier by a tight-hypergraph certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent completion through the masking-map Jacobian, determinantal circuits, and stresses, then prove generic closure properties algebraically.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem likewise asks whether missing coordinates are invariant along fibers of a low-rank observation map, although its observations are cohort laws rather than revealed entries.

method_exemplars.technique: Use sparse-hypergraph matroid rank and pebble moves to recognize and extract spanning tight subhypergraphs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once anchor-relation rows are shown to represent the (1,2)-sparsity matroid, this machinery directly yields the requested certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate cohort loading subspaces by covariance PCA, align them across overlapping masks, and derive fixed-T large-N limit theory for recovered means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates the same short-panel counterfactual mean functionals and supplies the natural estimation rung after exact identification.

open_problems.open_problem: Does every nonempty rank-two relation-margin shell contain fixed-radius admissible deformation pairs whose observed-law divergence is O(Nd²s²) while their missing-mean separation is of order d?

source_refs.excerpt: Replace the undefined relative-interior clause by explicit strict slack conditions for every class constraint
the lower experiment did not establish legal perturbations inside the model class

open_problems.why_unsolved: The earlier Ferrers-panel lower construction assumed an undefined relative-interior sequence and never established a positive legal perturbation radius. On a prescribed singular shell, an algebraically useful factor/loading deformation can leave the shell, collapse a signal eigengap, violate covariance or moment bounds, or fail at boundary baselines. The missing first step is a uniform slack-budget argument controlling every maintained constraint and the relation singular value simultaneously, rather than an interior-only local calculation.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A quantitative deformation lemma giving shell-independent legality constants, two-sided control s(P_d) in [s_N,2s_N], KL(P_d,P_0) <= KNd²s_N², and missing-target separation at least cd for every nonempty shell.

writing_exemplar.why: Its recoverability-versus-nonrecoverability framing explains why an algebraic null direction must be lifted to an admissible causal-panel pair before it supports a statistical converse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observation masks create low-rank null directions -> a null direction implies causal ambiguity only if it lifts to legal models -> quantitative lower bounds require legal pairs throughout shrinking singular shells.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct local low-rank alternatives aligned with the least-conditioned recovery direction and control their observed Gaussian divergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired lemma uses the same local-alternative geometry but must additionally preserve the causal model's full law, moment restrictions, exact rank, and prescribed shell.

method_exemplars.technique: Turn a target-relevant null direction of the masked low-rank observation operator into a nonrecoverability witness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The shell lemma is the quantitative and model-legal strengthening of that qualitative null-direction argument.

open_problems.open_problem: Over identifiable rank-two panels with relation singular margin s in [s_N,2s_N], is the minimax squared sup-norm risk for all missing untreated means of exact order min{1,1/(N s_N²)}, with consistency if and only if N s_N² diverges?

source_refs.claim: They prove regular fixed-T recovery and asymptotic normality under sufficient overlap, not a drifting-to-singularity minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Lihua Lei and Brad Ross

source_refs.claim: They obtain debiased MNAR matrix-completion inference under weak signals, but in a large-matrix regime with incoherence and missing-block restrictions.
source_refs.author: Jungjun Choi and Ming Yuan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Zhu derives minimax and adaptivity results for weak factor models, showing sharp inferential changes with factor strength.
source_refs.author: Yinchu Zhu

source_refs.excerpt: the deterministic staggered-mask singular-subspace bound, and the open-class lower-bound witness
a rate-optimal certificate and a matching all-procedure lower bound for arbitrary admissible wedges remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published short-panel counterfactual theory is regular-point asymptotics, while weak-factor and weak-signal completion results concern different targets or growing-matrix regimes. Prior CausalSmith attempts supplied the reciprocal-singular-value perturbation upper heuristic but no invariant observable margin or legal open-class lower experiment beyond a balanced rank-one benchmark. The lower bound must preserve the complete observed law restrictions, exact rank, covariance positivity, moment radius, and the same singular shell while producing target separation along a least-conditioned relation direction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower minimax bounds of order min{1,1/(N s_N²)} for squared sup-norm loss, an explicit covariance-PCA/APM least-squares estimator attaining the upper bound, and a theorem that uniform consistency holds exactly when N s_N² tends to infinity.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the exact destination—recovering average counterfactual outcomes from fixed-T panels—and supplies the regular benchmark refined by singular-margin theory.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Short panels require cross-cohort low-rank recovery -> spectral alignment identifies missing means under overlap -> near rank loss the recovery map becomes unstable -> determine the exact minimax risk and consistency boundary.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct factor-strength-indexed parameter spaces, derive local minimax lower bounds, and pair them with adaptive spectral estimators.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems index difficulty by a vanishing latent spectral quantity, but the requested modulus concerns missing causal means under deterministic masks.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine local low-rank regressions with instance-specific perturbation bounds and local minimax experiments for missing entries.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired rate is a deterministic-mask, causal-functional analogue of instance-optimal missing-entry recovery.

method_exemplars.technique: Relate local uniqueness and stability to transversality between the masking affine space and the rank-r tangent space.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The reciprocal relation margin should be the quantitative form of the same loss-of-transversality mechanism.

open_problems.open_problem: Over the same singular-margin shells, is every level-(1-alpha) uniformly honest simultaneous rectangle forced to have maximal half-width of order min{1,1/(sqrt(N)s_N)}, and can observed-moment confidence-set inversion attain that width?

source_refs.claim: They establish uniformly valid tests and confidence sets over weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences for broad extremum models.
source_refs.author: Donald W. K. Andrews and Xu Cheng

source_refs.claim: Uniform validity over unknown factor strength can require nonshrinking confidence intervals, exposing a validity-efficiency tension near weak factors.
source_refs.author: Yinchu Zhu

source_refs.claim: Their fixed-T estimator has regular asymptotic normality but does not provide shortest honest rectangles over shrinking relation margins.
source_refs.author: Lihua Lei and Brad Ross

source_refs.excerpt: the deterministic staggered-mask singular-subspace bound, and the open-class lower-bound witness
Replace the binary positive-Gram/no-Gram split with a strength-indexed class whose pre-period Gram may decay

open_problems.why_unsolved: Pointwise delta-method rectangles from covariance PCA cease to be uniform when inversion amplifies estimation noise by 1/s. Generic weak-identification inversion does not exploit the finite polynomial system of cohort moments or establish optimal simultaneous sup-norm width, while the prior panel proposals proved only endpoint or balanced-mask results and lacked legal lower pairs throughout the decaying-margin regime. The unresolved proof boundary consists of a shell-preserving testing lower bound for rectangle width and a feasible moment-set inversion whose coverage survives estimated eigenspaces and boundary configurations.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax lower bound and an attaining moment-inversion procedure proving uniform simultaneous coverage and maximal rectangle half-width of order min{1,1/(sqrt(N)s_N)} over every nonempty shell.

writing_exemplar.why: Its causal-panel formulation keeps the inferential target on missing untreated means and provides the regular intervals whose failure near singularity motivates robust inversion.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: General masks make counterfactual means a spectral recovery problem -> regular asymptotic normality supports conventional intervals -> vanishing relation margins invalidate pointwise linearization -> construct shortest rectangles honest across the weak-identification frontier.

method_exemplars.technique: Index stochastic criterion expansions by identification strength and invert identification-robust tests uniformly over drifting sequences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The relation singular value is the identification-strength parameter, and inversion avoids dividing by an unstable estimated relation.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias low-rank completion estimators, prove entrywise distributional approximations, and construct simultaneous confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete missing-entry inference template whose random-sampling and regular-conditioning arguments must be replaced by deterministic masks and shell-uniform inversion.

method_exemplars.technique: Use covariance PCA, subspace alignment, and fixed-T influence expansions for counterfactual matrix means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These estimated cohort moments and alignments are the natural inputs to the proposed confidence-set inversion.

open_problems.open_problem: For fixed rank r at least three and deterministic cohort masks, do (r+1)-element anchors yield a spanning-tight-hypergraph characterization of model-wide counterfactual recovery, or does an explicit mask show that no count-only sparsity matroid can represent the required relations?

source_refs.claim: They give efficiently verifiable deterministic conditions for finite and unique rank-r matrix completion, but not a universal tight-hypergraph equivalence.
source_refs.author: Daniel L. Pimentel-Alarcón, Nigel Boston, and Robert D. Nowak
source_refs.venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Signal Processing

source_refs.claim: They derive rank-r sparsity necessities and circuit or stress sufficiency rather than a count-only characterization for arbitrary rank.
source_refs.author: Franz J. Király, Louis Theran, and Ryota Tomioka

source_refs.claim: They obtain combinatorial rank-two completability results for special bipartite graph families, underscoring the difficulty of general higher-rank characterizations.
source_refs.author: Bill Jackson, Tibor Jordán, and Shin-ichi Tanigawa

open_problems.why_unsolved: Targeted searches found deterministic rank-r completion criteria and abstract pebble algorithms but no cohort-law recovery theorem identifying a higher-rank relation matroid with a count-only sparsity matroid. The first rank-two step that changes is the reduction of each cohort to scalar triple-anchor relations: at rank r these become determinant or Plücker relations with nontrivial syzygies. A valid extension therefore requires either a representation theorem incorporating those dependencies or a circuit demonstrating that every proposed count rule is insufficient.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an iff rank-r recovery theorem with a polynomial-time hypergraph or matroid certificate, or an explicit deterministic-mask counterexample followed by the correct determinantal-circuit characterization.

writing_exemplar.why: Its rank-agnostic short-panel framing naturally motivates testing whether a clean rank-two mask certificate survives with additional latent factors.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Low-rank structure links incompletely observed cohorts -> rank two may reduce alignment to triple relations -> empirical factor models often use more than two factors -> determine whether the certificate scales or encounters a determinantal obstruction.

method_exemplars.technique: Compute algebraic-matroid closure through Jacobian rank, circuit polynomials, and stress supports.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These tools can certify higher-rank dependencies even when cardinality inequalities do not characterize the determinantal matroid.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert rank-r subspace identifiability into efficiently checkable deterministic sampling conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its columnwise deterministic-mask analysis is structurally close to cohort-specific observed-time sets.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate and align rank-r covariance eigenspaces and derive limit theory for completed counterfactual means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the estimation rung after a correct higher-rank mask certificate identifies the missing means.

open_problems.open_problem: When the rank-two pebble condition fails, what is the sharp identified set for the vector of missing untreated cohort-time means under bounded positive loading covariances and common moment restrictions?

source_refs.claim: Manski develops identification regions for means and other distributional features under missing data rather than imposing point identification.
source_refs.author: Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Their algebraic framework distinguishes finite, unique, and non-completability but does not characterize sharp causal sets under covariance and moment restrictions.
source_refs.author: Franz J. Király, Louis Theran, and Ryota Tomioka

source_refs.claim: They estimate criterion-defined identified sets and construct confidence regions by inversion, including models with missing or corrupted data.
source_refs.author: Victor Chernozhukov, Han Hong, and Elie Tamer

open_problems.why_unsolved: A pair of nonidentification countermodels establishes only that the identified set is not a singleton. Generic missing-data bounds discard rank-two restrictions, while determinantal completion theory ordinarily asks only whether coordinates are finite or unique and does not impose complete observed-law compatibility, positive cohort loading covariances, or a common moment radius. The concrete obstacle is eliminating latent factors, rotations, loadings, and error laws from a constrained polynomial moment system while preserving sharpness mask by mask.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp semialgebraic characterization of the missing-mean identified set, finite programs for its support-function endpoints, and uniformly valid confidence regions obtained by inversion of observed cohort-moment restrictions.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the canonical motivation for replacing unjustified point recovery by the sharp implications of the observed data and credible restrictions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Missing outcomes defeat unrestricted point identification -> maintained restrictions can shrink the compatible set -> low-rank cohort geometry supplies strong restrictions -> characterize the sharp set when the pebble certificate fails.

method_exemplars.technique: Use determinantal ideals, circuit polynomials, and observation-map fibers to describe compatible low-rank completions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired causal identified set is the projection of an analogous compatibility fiber augmented by cohort covariance and full-law restrictions.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent an identified set through a population criterion and invert its sample analogue using resampling to obtain confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once low-rank compatibility is reduced to finite moment equalities and inequalities, criterion inversion provides the natural honest-inference rung.

literature_map:
Lei and Ross (2023, arXiv:2312.07520) is the closest anchor: fixed-T, large-N spectral identification and asymptotic normality for counterfactual matrix means under general cohort missingness.
Athey, Bayati, Doudchenko, Imbens, and Khosravi (2021, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2021.1891924) connect causal panels, interactive fixed effects, and nuclear-norm completion, but work in a regularized estimation regime.
Bai and Ng (2021/2023, arXiv:1910.06677) develop tall-wide factor imputation and normal theory under strong factors and block-style missingness.
Liu, Wang, and Xu (2024, AJPS, DOI 10.1111/ajps.12723) place interactive-fixed-effect and matrix-completion estimators in an applied counterfactual-imputation workflow.
Agarwal, Dahleh, Shah, and Shen (2023, COLT, arXiv:2109.15154) give causal-MNAR identification, consistency, and asymptotic normality through synthetic nearest neighbors.
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA, DOI 10.1080/01621459.2024.2380105) obtain debiased MNAR completion inference under weak signals, but with growing-matrix and incoherence restrictions.
Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan (2019, PNAS, arXiv:1906.04159) give debiased entrywise inference under random sampling and regular conditioning.
Király, Theran, and Tomioka (2015, JMLR, arXiv:1211.4116) supply determinantal-matroid tools: Jacobian closure, stresses, circuits, and generic entry completability.
Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak (2016, IEEE JSTSP, arXiv:1503.02596) give deterministic rank-r completion conditions but not a causal full-law iff theorem.
Jackson, Jordán, and Tanigawa (2014, SIAM J. Discrete Math., DOI 10.1137/140960098) obtain combinatorial completability results for special rank-two graph families.
Streinu and Theran (2009, European J. Combinatorics, arXiv:math/0703921) characterize sparse hypergraphs and provide pebble recognition and extraction algorithms.
Shapiro, Xie, and Zhang (2019, IEEE TSP, arXiv:1802.00047) connect deterministic completion stability to tangent-space transversality.
Zhu (2019, arXiv:1910.10382) establishes minimax and honesty phenomena under weak factors, but not deterministic-mask causal counterfactual recovery.
Andrews and Cheng (2012, Econometrica, DOI 10.3982/ECTA9456) and Forneron (2024, Journal of Econometrics, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2023.105552) provide weak-identification-robust inversion and singular-Jacobian diagnostics.
The targeted searches leave the combinatorial cohort-law bridge, shell-preserving causal lower experiment, and optimal honest rectangle as an apparently unoccupied intersection.
